meta.description: Download raw sequencing reads from NCBI SRA using sra-tools (prefetch, fasterq-dump, vdb-validate) or the ENA mirror. Use when pulling FASTQ for SRR/ERR/DRR accessions, deciding between SRA-direct, ENA mirror, or AWS/GCP cloud mirror (STRIDES), handling --include-technical for 10x and other single-cell records, validating with MD5/vdb-validate, navigating SRR/SRX/SRS/SRP/PRJNA hierarchy, or finding accessions via pysradb. Encodes SRA cloud-egress economics, the fasterq-dump uncompressed-scratch trap, and the --max-size default that silently truncates large prefetches.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs/p-values/sample sizes in any of the 9 outputs; the Skill only moves real, verifiable sequencing data. Unchanged from pre-fix.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive medical conclusions in any output; Input 6 stays a data-access-boundary question, not a medical-advice one. Unchanged from pre-fix.

methodological_ground.detail: The pre-fix FAIL was for a complete, grep-confirmed absence of dbGaP/controlled-access/ethical-compliance guidance. That gap is closed: SKILL.md now has a full 'Controlled-access (dbGaP) data' section (recognition signals, why this unauthenticated Skill is out of scope, the real --ngc <repository-key>.ngc mechanism, and an explicit stop-and-ask boundary), confirmed by direct reading, plus a matching Common-errors row. Caveat (does not re-fire M3, which is about the warning being present, not about code enforcement): Input 8 found that the shipped code does not reliably surface the section's own documented recognition signal (an ENA response omitting fastq_ftp) -- see code_usability and recommendation P1-1.

code_usability.detail: The pre-fix FAIL was 100% failure (4/4 real accessions) on the Skill's own flagship code path. That path now succeeds on 6/6 real live accessions tested in this re-audit (2 regression + 4 the fixer never used) plus a clean 3/3 batch run; all shipped scripts pass bash -n / py_compile. Caveat (does not re-fire M4, whose trigger is code being unrunnable -- this code runs and is correct for its documented, verified use case): a real, narrower edge case was found and verified by direct execution -- see Input 8 and recommendation P1-1.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness now 4/4 (controlled-access use case closed). Correctness up from 1/4 to 3/4: the flagship ENA snippet is verified correct on 6/6 real accessions, but Input 8 found a genuine correctness gap when ENA omits a requested field (false-positive 'md5 OK' with zero files downloaded). Appropriateness unchanged, 3/4.

reliability.note: Up from 4/12. The common failure modes (network errors, wrong accession) are handled well and were praised pre-fix; this re-audit's own execution (input8/8b/8c/8d) found one specific edge case -- ENA omitting a requested field -- that still fails badly: silently in the inline SKILL.md snippet (false 'md5 OK'), and as a full-batch abort (not a per-accession skip) in download_batch.sh, bypassing that script's own pre-existing continue-on-failure guard.

performance_context.note: Unchanged. SKILL.md grew from 372 to 417 lines (still under the 500-line guideline) with no references/ split; usage-guide.md's redundancy pass (82 -> 54 lines) helped token cost slightly but not enough to move the score.

agent_usability.note: Up from 11/16. Common-errors table now documents both the ENA column-selection failure mode and the dbGaP authorization-error case (both were gaps pre-fix). Does not yet document the false-success ('md5 OK' with no files) failure mode this re-audit found.

human_usability.note: Up from 5/8. Discoverability stays 4/4. Forgiveness up from 1/4 to 2/4: the common failure mode is no longer misleading, but the omitted-field edge case is worse than 'misleading' in the single-accession script -- it reports false success rather than any visible error.

security.note: Unchanged. No hardcoded secrets, no eval/exec of raw strings; accession-format validation before interpolation into curl/prefetch still absent (out of scope for this fix pass).

maintainability.note: Up from 9/12. The redundancy pass removed real duplication between usage-guide.md and SKILL.md (one genuinely new fact, aws-cli install, was correctly relocated rather than dropped) and fixed a pre-existing Related-Skills drift bug (bwa-alignment link was in usage-guide.md but missing from SKILL.md).

agent_specific.note: Up from 15/20. Escape Hatches up from 1/4 to 3/4: a real dbGaP stop-and-ask boundary and a >~10GB download confirmation instruction now exist. Not 4/4 because the boundary is advisory text only -- Input 8 shows the shipped code can't reliably help an agent notice when it applies. Trigger Precision and Composability remain strong (4/4).

key_strengths: The flagship ENA-mirror code path, previously broken 100% of the time (4/4 real accessions pre-fix), now succeeds reliably: verified on 6/6 real live accessions in this re-audit (2 regression accessions the pre-fix audit and fixer used, plus 4 the fixer never used) and a clean 3/3 batch run -- zero real-world download failures observed in this audit.

The new 'Controlled-access (dbGaP) data' section is accurate and actionable: real recognition signals, the actual --ngc mechanism, and an explicit stop-and-ask boundary, closing a documentation gap that was previously a complete, grep-confirmed absence.

The fixer's correction of the pysradb total_size claim is independently verified correct via pysradb's own source code (not just re-asserted), directly refuting the original pre-fix audit's 'no byte-size column' claim.

The ENA-vs-SRA-direct read-count divergence note is now correctly framed as 'can differ' rather than 'always differs' -- independently confirmed with a fresh accession (ERR10015134) where the two sources agreed exactly (14,541 = 14,541), unlike the originally-flagged ERR10419835.
SRA-toolkit path (prefetch/vdb-validate/fasterq-dump) and pysradb accession-resolution logic remain correct and were untouched by the fix, as expected.

recommendations.title: Header-based ENA column lookup fails ungracefully when a requested field is genuinely absent
recommendations.problem: The fix correctly makes the ENA-mirror column lookup name-based instead of position-based, but neither the inline SKILL.md snippet nor examples/download_batch.sh guards the case where the requested field (e.g. fastq_ftp) is simply not in the response -- exactly the scenario the Skill's own new dbGaP section names as a recognition signal. The inline snippet (no set -e, no empty-column guard) silently reports a false-positive 'md5 OK' with zero files downloaded. download_batch.sh aborts the ENTIRE batch (not just the one bad accession) because set -euo pipefail plus grep -nx's non-match exit status fires before the script's own pre-existing 'if [ -z "${URLS}" ]' continue-on-failure guard is ever reached.
recommendations.root_cause: FTP_COL/MD5_COL are computed via a pipeline that can legitimately exit non-zero (grep -nx no match) with no guard immediately after, before URLS/MD5S are derived from them.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit check right after computing FTP_COL/MD5_COL in both the SKILL.md inline snippet and download_batch.sh: if either is empty, print a clear, accession-attributed message (e.g. pointing at the 'Controlled-access (dbGaP) data' section) and, in the batch script, 'continue' to the next accession rather than letting the pipeline's exit status trigger set -e mid-batch.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md's dbGaP boundary is advisory text only; no shipped script surfaces its own documented recognition signal
recommendations.problem: The 'Controlled-access (dbGaP) data' section correctly tells an agent to recognize an omitted fastq_ftp field as a controlled-access signal, but no shipped script actually detects or names that condition in its output -- see P1-1, which shows the current behavior actively obscures it in one script and crashes opaquely in the other.
recommendations.root_cause: The boundary was added as documentation in the same pass that also fixed the column-index bug, without connecting the two: the new prose describes a signal the (also-changed) code doesn't yet surface.
recommendations.fix: Once P1-1's guard is added, point its error message directly at the 'Controlled-access (dbGaP) data' section, so the code and the documentation reinforce each other instead of the documentation describing a signal the code silently swallows.

recommendations.title: SRA-toolkit path evidence relies on native binaries run directly, not the shipped download_single.sh wrapper end-to-end
recommendations.problem: This re-audit (like the pre-fix one) verified prefetch/vdb-validate/fasterq-dump via direct native-binary calls in PowerShell rather than running examples/download_single.sh itself end-to-end, because of the known git-bash/MSYS fasterq-dump segfault. The script's pigz->gzip fallback was only syntax-checked (bash -n), not exercised.
recommendations.root_cause: Platform-specific shell incompatibility (MSYS path handling) with fasterq-dump, pre-existing and outside this fix's scope.
recommendations.fix: No Skill change needed; note for future auditors to run download_single.sh's compression step specifically (not just the raw toolkit calls) when a non-MSYS shell is available, to get one full end-to-end confirmation of the pigz fallback in context.
